At that time, when the assembly of devas had heard these verses, eighty-four thousand devas of the Cāturmahārājika heaven, hundreds of thousands of Trāyastriṃśa devas, hundreds of thousands of Yāma devas, hundreds of thousands of Tuṣita devas, hundreds of thousands of Nirmāṇarati devas, hundreds of thousands of Paranirmitavaśavartin devas, sixty thousand Māra devas, and sixty-eight thousand Brahmakāyika devas who had accumulated merit in previous lives, as well as devas from up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven and countless hundreds of thousands of other devas—such as these who were already present in the assembly—furthermore, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas from the other directions: east, west, south, north, the four intermediate points, and above and below, all gathered there together.
At that time, a preeminent son of heaven within the great assembly spoke in verse:
“You all should now listen: I have given rise to a resolute mind, Abandoning desire and supernormal powers, As well as the joys of the various dhyānas and samādhis.”
Following the Most Victorious One, from the moment of his descent into the mother’s womb,
we shall not allow any evils to invade him, but shall always provide protection.
With various exquisite music, we shall praise and recite the ocean of his merits.
Causing devas and humans to rejoice, they inspire the mind set on the unsurpassed path.
Having heard this, devas and humans rejoice and eliminate their manifold afflictions;
they scatter *māndārava* flowers, *candra*, *candraprabha*, and others.
And by burning aloeswood incense, one makes offerings to those of pure merit.
"While the Bodhisattva dwells within the womb, he is not defiled by the three impurities;
transcending birth, old age, and death, he attains the guidance that reaches the ultimate limit."
With pure minds, we follow the one endowed with wisdom.
When Śakra, Brahmā, and the other celestial kings saw him take seven steps,
they cupped their hands in fragrant water and bathed this stainless Sage.
Following all that is done in accordance with the world, humans and devas obtain great merit.
Remaining ever unstained while dwelling amidst desire, you have transcended the city and renounced your precious throne;
we vow to follow after you.
Subduing Māra and attaining perfect enlightenment, you exhorted others with the subtle and wondrous Dharma;
your Buddha-activities pervaded the three realms, and the nectar of immortality saturated all living beings.
Even until their entry into nirvana, you were ever present, never for a moment abandoning them.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“When the countless goddesses of the desire realm saw that the Bodhisattva’s physical form and marks were subtle and wondrous and that he was about to descend to be born, each of them said:
‘What kind of woman should give birth to the Bodhisattva?’”
"There must surely be one of supreme virtue worthy of harboring the Honored One.

All were filled with admiration and a heart of reverent love; through the karmic rewards of their own merit, they attained supernatural powers and the body of *manomayakāya*, traveling from that celestial palace to the city of Kapilavastu in a single instant.

The city of Kapilavastu was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of parks, groves, ponds, and pools, adorned with extraordinary splendor like the palace of Śakra. Within that palace was a great hall named Dhṛtarāṣṭra, where the noble Queen Māyā resided; it was exquisitely decorated and beautifully furnished, pure and stainless, radiant with majestic power.
The Noble Queen was adorned with necklaces and draped in celestial garments, her body embellished with various exquisite jewels.
When the goddesses arrived at this palace, they remained in the air, gazing upon the Noble Queen.
And there is a verse that says:
"The celestial maidens of the desire realm, beholding the wondrous body of the Bodhisattva,
all form this thought:"
"What kind of people were the Bodhisattva’s mothers?
Competing with one another, they carried flower garlands and the like, as well as ointments and powdered incense;
with joyful hearts they went to the royal palace, joining their palms in reverent homage."
In exquisite robes and beautiful countenance, they all extended their hands and pointed together, seeing him seated upon a sublime jeweled throne; with virtuous minds, they observed him intently:
"Such a wondrous form as this exists among humans, but has never before been seen in the heavens."
We have always considered ourselves the most excellent among the celestial maidens;
yet now that we behold this person, a sense of self-contempt arises within us.
Adorned with supreme merit, his countenance is exceedingly upright and handsome.
Were it not for these supreme virtues, who else could be worthy to be the mother of a Bodhisattva?
Just as a priceless jewel is placed within a pure vessel of precious gems,
so too is the mother of a Bodhisattva worthy to conceive one of such supreme virtue.
Those who see him give rise to joy, their minds never wearying of him.
His countenance is most upright and handsome, his physical marks exceedingly radiant;
like the moon in the void, beholding him, one’s mind becomes pure.
Like the sun’s intense radiance, like pure gold refined a hundred times—seeing that mother of the Bodhisattva, her brilliance was likewise so.
Her hair was fragrant, soft, and lustrous; deep black, it resembled the hue of a bumblebee.
His bright teeth are like stars in the void; his eyes are like the petals of the blue lotus.
His limbs move with perfect grace, and his hands and feet are entirely level and upright.
Even among the gods there is no peer; who in the human world could compare with him?
Having observed thus, they circumambulated her to the right, scattering incense and flowers;
praising the Mother of Buddhas by name, they returned to the heavens.
At that time, the four world-protectors, Śakra, Brahmā, and the gods of the desire realm [did likewise].
Together with the other eight assemblies, they all came to protect the Mother of the Buddha.
Having all seen that the Bodhisattva was about to descend to be born,
the devas brought exquisite incense and flowers and joyfully approached to stand before her.
With palms joined and heads bowed in prostration, they entreated him: "The time for your descent has arrived;
O Lion-King of Eloquence, out of compassion, please take birth in the world.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:

"When the Bodhisattva was about to descend to be born, there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas in the eastern direction, all of whom were in their final birth before enlightenment (ekajātipratibaddha), who came to the Tuṣita Heaven palace to make offerings to the Bodhisattva. Likewise, those in their final birth before enlightenment in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below, all arrived at the Tuṣita Heaven palace to make offerings to the Bodhisattva.

Furthermore, from the worlds of the ten directions—the Cāturmahārājakāyika, Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens—each accompanied by eighty-four thousand celestial maidens, surrounded him from front and behind, arrived at the Tuṣita palace, and made offerings to the Bodhisattva with drums, music, stringed instruments, and song."

At that time, the Bodhisattva was dwelling in a great celestial palace, seated upon a lion throne of supreme treasury born of manifold virtues; surrounded by those bodhisattvas and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of devas, who offered him worship, reverence, respect, and praise, he then descended from the most excellent Tuṣita heaven to take birth.

"When he is about to descend to be born, he emits an unprecedented radiance from his physical form that illuminates the entire trichiliocosm; even those dark and obscure regions between worlds, which the majestic light of the sun and moon cannot reach, become brilliantly bright."
The sentient beings therein were each able to see one another and all spoke these words: "How is it that sentient beings have suddenly appeared here?

At that time, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways with eighteen aspects: namely, shaking, intense shaking, and universal shaking; striking, intense striking, and universal striking; shifting, intense shifting, and universal shifting; surging upward and collapsing downward, intense surging and collapsing, and universal surging and collapsing; emitting sound, intense emission of sound, and universal emission of sound; surging at the edges and subsiding in the center, surging in the center and subsiding at the edges; surging in the east and subsiding in the west, surging in the west and subsiding in the east; surging in the south and subsiding in the north, and surging in the north and subsiding in the south.
At that time, all sentient beings were filled with joy and exultation; they delighted in supreme, pure happiness and offered praises and eulogies.

When they heard these sounds, not a single sentient being felt fear or alarm. The majestic radiance of Brahmā, Śakra, the World Protectors, the sun, and the moon all ceased to appear, while all those in the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts, as well as all other sentient beings, received peace and security.

At this time, not a single sentient being was oppressed by any of the afflictions such as greed, hatred, or delusion; instead, they felt mutual compassion and a mind of altruism toward one another, regarding each other as fathers, mothers, elder brothers, or younger brothers.

The musical instruments of humans and devas resounded spontaneously without being struck; immeasurable devas bore this wondrous pavilion upon their heads and supported it with their hands, while hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens surrounded it from front and back, performing divine music.
From within the sounds of that music, these sublime verses emerged, extolling the Bodhisattva:
“O Venerable One, through long nights you have accumulated and practiced; All your pure deeds are now fully perfected.
Abiding in the truly supreme principle, You now receive the highest offerings of gods and humans.”
In the past, throughout immeasurable koṭis of kalpas, he was able to give away even his beloved wife and children;
because he practiced such generosity, he obtained this supreme retribution and thus receives these exquisite celestial flowers and perfumes.
He cut flesh from his own body and weighed it out, Out of compassion saving that dove on the verge of death;
Furthermore, by practicing dāna, he obtained a supreme reward, Able to bring satisfaction to the hungry ghosts.
In the past, across boundless eons, the Venerable One firmly maintained the pure precepts without ever violating them;
by virtue of that ethical discipline, he obtained a supreme reward, which is able to cause all afflictions in the evil realms to cease.
In the past, across boundless eons, the Venerable One practiced patience for the sake of seeking enlightenment;
through that *kṣānti*, he obtained a supreme reward, enabling humans and devas to regard one another with mutual compassion.
The Venerable One, throughout boundless kalpas of the past, Cultivated supreme diligence without ceasing;
Through that diligent exertion, he obtained a sublime reward: His physical form is as majestic and upright as Mount Sumeru.
In boundless kalpas of the past, the Venerable One cultivated various meditative absorptions to sever the fetters and latent tendencies;
by virtue of those dhyānas, he attained a supreme retribution, enabling him to be free from afflictions in this present life.
The Venerable One, throughout boundless kalpas of the past, Cultivated wisdom and severed all fetters;
By means of that *prajñā*, he attained this supreme retribution, Able to cause his radiance to be exceedingly pure.
Donning the armor of loving-kindness to eliminate afflictions, And manifesting in this world out of compassion for all beings, You have realized the supreme, wondrous equanimity;
I pay homage to the Venerable One who has attained the Brahma-abodes.
Illuminating with the torch of the light of wisdom, Purifying the darkness of ignorance and all faults,
Lord of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system— I take refuge in the Muni, the Great Guide.
Possessing supreme wisdom and supernormal powers, you have attained all the higher knowledges; seeing the true meaning, you are able to manifest it for others.
Having yourself attained liberation, you can rescue all beings; I take refuge in the Captain who enables one to cross over.
Conforming to worldly ways, he appears as an ordinary being, yet remains unstained by worldly dharmas.
If any sentient beings should hear or see him, they will obtain inconceivable and supreme benefits;
how much more so for those who hear the sublime and wondrous Dharma—through faith and joy, they shall give rise to vast goodness.
The Tuṣita Heaven palace is shrouded in darkness, while in Jambudvīpa the sun is about to rise;
for all sentient beings who slumber in the torpor of afflictions, may the Venerable One cause them all to awaken.
The city of Kapilavastu flourished even more, surrounded by immeasurable hosts of devas;
celestial jewel-women played heavenly music, their wondrous sounds resonating throughout the royal city.
The Mother of Buddhas is adorned with exquisite beauty; her majestic presence arises from pure karma.
The Noble Son is upright and most extraordinary, his radiance illuminating the trichiliocosm.
All sentient beings dwelling in that land Are entirely free from the afflictions of contention and dispute;
With hearts of universal compassion, they respect and accord with one another— All this is due to the majestic power of the Bodhisattva.
The royal lineage of King Śuddhodana shall flourish; by this merit, he shall succeed as a Wheel-Turning Monarch (Cakravartin).
All the treasuries within his city shall be filled to overflowing with every kind of precious jewel.
Yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kumbhāṇḍas, asuras, guhyakas, and the hosts of devas,
protect the dwelling place of the Bodhisattva; before long, they shall all realize liberation and dedicate it entirely to the path of bodhi,
vowing to swiftly attain perfect enlightenment just like the Honored One.
6. Chapter on Dwelling in the Womb. The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:

"After the winter solstice had passed, during the spring equinox in the month of Vaiśākha, when the flowers and leaves of the groves were fresh, lustrous, and lovely, and it was neither cold nor hot; at the conjunction of the lunar mansion Rohiṇī, the Supreme Person of the Three Realms observed that the world was bright and the moon was full and pure, while the Puṣya star was precisely in conjunction with the moon."

At that time, the Bodhisattva descended from the Tuṣita heaven and entered his mother’s womb in the form of a white elephant, complete with six tusks; those tusks were golden in color and its head was suffused with a crimson light. Its physical features and all its faculties were perfectly complete; with right mindfulness and full awareness, it descended and entered through the mother’s right side.
"At that time, the Holy Queen was sleeping peacefully, and within her dream she witnessed such a thing.
Then, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"The Supreme Being took birth as a white elephant, Pure and bright as snow, endowed with six tusks."
His nose, feet, and head were exquisite, with a crimson radiance; his limbs and features were all perfectly complete.
He descended from the right side of her flank as if in play, causing the Buddha’s mother to rejoice exceedingly.
Having never before seen or heard of such a thing, her body and mind were as tranquil and secure as in meditative concentration.

At that time, the Noble Consort’s body and mind were filled with universal joy; immediately upon her seat, she adorned her person with various exquisite jewels. Surrounded by countless maidservants in respectful attendance, she descended from the magnificent palace and proceeded to the Aśoka Garden.
Having arrived at that garden, he sent a messenger to inform King Śuddhodana, saying:
"I wish to see you; Your Majesty should come for a brief moment.

Upon hearing this message, the king’s heart was filled with great joy. Rising from his jeweled throne, he set out for the Aśoka Garden accompanied by his ministers, officials, and retinue, who escorted him from before and behind.
Having reached the gate of the garden, his entire body became heavy and he was unable to move forward, whereupon he spoke this verse:
"Recalling when I went against my powerful enemies, Even then my body was not so heavy;
Now it has suddenly become thus— To whom shall I ask about this change?"
Then, a devaputra from the Śuddhāvāsa heaven manifested his upper body in the sky and spoke these verses to King Śuddhodana:
“The Bodhisattva of great majesty has descended from the Tuṣita palace,
Entrusting himself to the womb of the Noble Queen to become the king’s eldest son.”
"All practices are fully perfected; Honored by humans and devas, Endowed with compassion, merit, and wisdom, You shall receive your office through consecration.
At that time, King Śuddhodana, having heard these verses, joined his palms, bowed his head in prostration, and spoke thus:
"I have now witnessed this rare and marvelous event.
Thereupon, he entered to see the Noble Queen; casting aside his pride and conceit, he approached her and asked:
"What do you seek?"
"I pray that you will explain this for me.
At that time, the Noble Queen replied with a verse:
"In my sleep and dream, I saw an elephant like white silver."
His radiance surpasses that of the sun and moon; his physical marks are exceedingly majestic and pure.
His six tusks possess awesome power, indestructible like vajra;
his limbs are most firm and beautiful as he enters my womb.
Since then, many auspicious signs have appeared; may Your Majesty now listen well.
I see the three thousandfold world-system as vast, magnificent, and beautifully adorned;
whenever I am asleep, the devas come to praise me.
Afflictions such as greed and hatred, along with all fetters and latent tendencies, have been extinguished;
my mind is in the bliss of tranquility, as if dwelling within meditative concentration.
It is fitting to summon a dream interpreter who clearly understands the Vedas.
"One well-versed in the laws of the eight luminaries, capable of discerning good and ill fortune—
summon that person quickly to interpret this dream for me.
When the king heard these words, he immediately summoned the dream-interpreters.
And he spoke to those people, saying:
"You should interpret the dream of the Noble Queen.
Then the Noble Queen informed them of the circumstances of her own dream.
"Since you claim to be skilled in divination, I shall now speak for you.
In my dream, there was an elephant as white as snow, surpassing the light of the sun and moon;
it possessed six tusks and its limbs were most majestic and beautiful."
Of wondrous form and supreme radiant purity, Firm and dense as a diamond, he has entered my womb;
Such was the event I saw in my dream.
When that person heard the Holy Queen recount the causes and conditions of her dream,
They all said:
"Nothing is not auspicious; this dream is most propitious.
Your lineage shall flourish and prosper, and you will surely give birth to a son of superior marks."
If remaining at home, he would become a Wheel-Turning King, ruling his realm through his majestic power;
But by leaving the home life, he will attain the Way of the Buddha, out of compassion for all the world.
He shall sprinkle the nectar of the Dharma, revered by humans and devas alike.

At that time, King Śuddhodana, having heard the brahmin’s explanation of the causes and conditions of the dream, was filled with great joy. He immediately bestowed upon him exquisite garments and various kinds of fine food, and sent him back to his own place.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"At that time, King Śuddhodana established a great assembly for giving at the crossroads of the four city gates for the sake of the Bodhisattva. To those who required food he gave food; to those who required clothing he gave clothing; and even for incense, flowers, bedding, fields, houses, vehicles, and whatever else was sought, he provided it all."
At that time, the King thought to himself:
"In which palace shall I establish the Noble Queen, so that she may dwell in joy and free from sorrow?
Then the Four Heavenly Kings came to the King's presence and spoke these words:
"May Your Majesty remain well and at ease; do not dwell upon this matter. I shall take a magnificent palace for the Bodhisattva.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, came to the King's presence and spoke these verses:
"The palaces of the World-Protectors are inferior, Unfit for the Noble Queen to inhabit;"
"The Trāyastriṃśa Heaven has a supreme palace; I bring it here to offer to the Bodhisattva.
At that time, the Yāma Devaputra again came to the King's presence and spoke in verse:
"I have a most excellent and wondrous palace, Surpassing even the palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."
"In that Yāma Heaven, we now offer it to the Bodhisattva.
Then the Devaputra of Tuṣita came again to the King’s presence and spoke in verse:
"The wondrous celestial palace of Tuṣita is where the Bodhisattva originally dwelt."
"This is most excellent; / I offer it back to the Bodhisattva.
Then the Son of Heaven from the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations came again to the King's presence and spoke in verse:
"I have a precious palace, / Produced according to my will."
"Adorned with supreme wonder, I pray that you accept it for the Bodhisattva.
Then the Devaputra of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations came again to the King's abode and spoke in verse:
"I possess a wondrous palace, surpassing all the heavens of desire."
Adorned with various jewels, pure and pleasing to the mind,
its radiance most wondrous and brilliant, with fragrant flowers scattered all around;
may this bring peace to the Noble Lady, and I bring it here to offer to the Bodhisattva.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"At that time, the devaputras of the desire realm, for the sake of making offerings, each brought their respective palaces to the palace of King Śuddhodana."
That king also constructed for the Bodhisattva a wondrous palace, exquisitely adorned and magnificent beyond anything found in the human world.

At that time, by the majestic spiritual power of the Great Adornment Samādhi, the Bodhisattva caused the body of the noble Queen Māyā to appear within all those palaces; in each, the Bodhisattva was seated in the full lotus posture against his mother’s right flank.
Each of the sons of the gods thought to themselves:
"The mother of the Bodhisattva dwells only in my palace.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“The Great Array Samādhi, with its inconceivable spiritual transformations,
brings joy to all the devas and fills the Father King with delight.
While this sutra was being spoken, there were among those in the assembly certain sons of gods who gave rise to these thoughts:

"If even the gods of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings hear of this human world’s filth and impurity, how much more so for those above them—the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, up to the Tuṣita Heaven and all the great devas?"

How is it that the Bodhisattva, a treasure of the world, most supreme, pure, exquisite, and fragrant, has abandoned the Tuṣita heaven to dwell among humans, remaining within his mother’s womb for ten months?
At that time, Ānanda, receiving the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, knelt with palms joined and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
The female body abounds in various desires and evils; how is it that when the Tathāgata was a bodhisattva, he abandoned Tuṣita Heaven and dwelt within his mother’s womb on her right side?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"When the Bodhisattva was formerly in his mother’s womb, he was not defiled by impurities; he constantly dwelt in a jeweled palace, most supremely adorned and pure."
"Do you wish to see such a jeweled palace?
I shall show it to you.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will deign to reveal [this teaching], so that all who behold it may give rise to joy.

At that time, the Tathāgata, by means of his supernatural power, caused Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, together with sixty hundred thousand koṭis of Brahmās, to descend from the heavens to Jambudvīpa and approach the place where the Buddha was. They paid homage with prostrations, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing [the answer] yet asking intentionally, addressed the Brahma King, saying:
"When I was formerly a bodhisattva, during the ten months I resided in the womb, where is the precious palace I occupied now?"
"You may bring it here.
Brahmā, King of the Gods, replied,
"It is currently in the Brahma-world."
Then the Lord of the Sahā World bowed his head in prostration and suddenly vanished. In an instant, he ascended to the Brahma palace and addressed the son of the Great Brahma, saying:
"You should descend in succession as far as the Heaven of the Thirty-three and cry out in a loud voice:
'Today the Brahma King intends to take the precious palace where the Tathāgata resided while in the womb back to the Buddha's presence. Those who wish to see it should come quickly.'"

At that time, the Brahmā King took the Bodhisattva’s palace and placed it within his own Brahmā palace. That Brahmā palace measured exactly three hundred yojanas in length and breadth; surrounded with reverence by eighty-four thousand koṭis of Brahmā devas, he descended from the Brahma-world to Jambudvīpa.

At that time, immeasurable devas from the desire realm all gathered like clouds at the place where the Tathāgata was, making offerings with celestial fine garments, various kinds of music, flower garlands, exquisite incense, and celestial ornaments.

At that time, from Śakra, Lord of the Devas, up to the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, none were ever able to behold the Bodhisattva’s palace; even though they scrutinized it closely, they could not see it.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings asked Śakra:
"By what means can we behold this palace? Śakra replied:
"You shall only be able to see him after you have invited the Tathāgata.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, together with the Four Heavenly Kings, bowed their heads and entreated the Buddha.
Then, Mahābrahmā, together with the various Brahmās, took up the Bodhisattva’s palace and placed it before the Buddha.

The palace was three stories high and adorned all around with the celestial fragrance of ox-head sandalwood; a single portion of this incense was worth as much as a trichiliocosm. It radiated brilliant light and was embellished with various celestial jewels. The couches, seats, and utensils were all suited to a bodhisattva, so subtle, exquisite, and magnificent that they were beyond anything found among humans or devas, save for the unique *sūrya-āvarta* (sun-turning) whorl mark of a bodhisattva.
The celestial garments worn by the Great Brahma King, when reaching the seat of the Bodhisattva, become like *kambala* cloth soaked in water.
Within his three palaces, there are pure and exquisite celestial flowers all around; these palaces are firm and indestructible.
Everything he touched or came near produced exquisite bliss, like the kācilinda garment;
all the celestial palaces of the desire realm appeared within the Bodhisattva’s precious palace.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"On the night the Bodhisattva entered the womb, from the depths of the water below, a lotus flower surged forth, piercing through the earth wheel and ascending as far as the Brahma world, measuring exactly sixty-eight lakṣas of yojanas in length and breadth. No one was able to see such a lotus, except for the Tathāgatas, the bodhisattvas, and the Great Brahmā King."

Within this trichiliocosm, all pure, sublime, and exquisite flavors—like nectar—manifested within these flowers. Mahābrahmā, using a vessel of vaidūrya, filled it with this pure and wondrous nectar-like flavor and offered it to the Bodhisattva; the Bodhisattva then accepted and partook of it.
"O Bhikṣus!

You should know that among the sentient beings of the world, there is none capable of consuming the flavor of such ambrosia, except for the Bodhisattvas in their final body at the ultimate stage of the tenth bhūmi who alone are able to consume it."
"O Bhikṣus! By what roots of goodness did the Bodhisattva experience this flavor?

It was because, in the long night of the past while practicing the bodhisattva path, he was able to provide medical treatment to relieve the suffering of illness, fulfill all desires and aspirations, and bestow fearlessness upon all who were terrified."

Furthermore, having made offerings of exquisite flowers and fruits to the Tathāgata, to the Buddha’s stūpas and shrines, to all the noble assemblies, and to one's parents and elders, one should only then partake of them oneself.

By virtue of this meritorious retribution, the Great Brahmā King constantly brings forth the flavor of ambrosia to offer within the precious palace; furthermore, through the power of the Bodhisattva’s original vows, exquisite garments, various ornaments, and all kinds of utensils can appear at will.

Ānanda! When all Bodhisattvas are about to enter the womb, there first appears before the mother’s right flank such a palace adorned with jewels; thereafter, they descend from the Tuṣita heaven and enter the womb, sitting cross-legged within this palace.

Ānanda! In all the worlds of the ten directions, every Queen Māyā likewise saw a white elephant coming in her dreams; Śakra Devendra and the Four Heavenly Kings, along with the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, all followed and protected her.
Furthermore, there were four celestial maidens:
the first was named Ukhalī, the second Mūkhalī, the third Dhvajāgryā, and the fourth Prabhavatī; they too, together with their retinues, constantly came to provide protection.

"At that time, while the Bodhisattva dwelt within his mother’s womb, the radiance of his physical form was like a great torch lit atop a mountain peak in the darkness of night, or like pure gold set within lapis lazuli; its brilliant light shone forth, pervading the entire world."

The Four Great Heavenly Kings, the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, and their retinues each morning made respectful offerings; they all saw the Bodhisattva comfort them with greetings, slowly raise his right hand to indicate a seat for them to sit upon, and preach the Dharma for them, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening them in a way they had never experienced before.

When he wished to depart, the Bodhisattva would slowly raise his right hand to bid him leave; Śakra-devānām-indra and the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven would prostrate, circumambulate, and take their leave.

At every midday, they would respectfully make offerings for the sake of hearing the Dharma; they all saw the Bodhisattva comfort and inquire after them, slowly raising his right hand to point to a seat and invite them to sit, preaching the Dharma for them to instruct, benefit, and gladden them, such that they attained what they had never experienced before.
When he wished to depart, the Bodhisattva would gently raise his right hand to dismiss him; [the visitor] would prostrate, circumambulate, take leave, and depart.

Every afternoon, Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Brahma-deva sons, would respectfully make offerings for the sake of hearing the Dharma; they all saw the Bodhisattva comfort and greet them, gently raising his right hand to point to a seat and bid them sit, preaching the Dharma for them to instruct, benefit, and gladden them, causing them to give rise to joy and a sense of the unprecedented.
When he wished to depart, the Bodhisattva slowly raised his right hand, signaling him to go; [the man] prostrated, circumambulated him, took his leave, and departed. "Ānanda!

From the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—throughout the ten directions—countless hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas have come here at sunset to pay respectful homage and to listen to the Dharma."
At that time, the Bodhisattva manifested a magnificently adorned lion throne and caused all the bodhisattvas to sit upon them, where they questioned one another and analyzed the Supreme Vehicle.
"These great bodhisattvas who have come here can be seen only by those who share the same practice and the same vehicle; even the noble Queen Māyā cannot see them. Ānanda!"

When the Bodhisattva was dwelling in the womb, he did not cause the Noble Queen’s body to feel heavy or oppressed by any suffering; she remained supple, light, at ease, serene, and joyful. She was free from the afflictions of desire, hatred, delusion, and feverish distress;
likewise, she was without thoughts of lust, thoughts of malice, or thoughts of harm.
Furthermore, she was free from cold or heat, hunger or thirst, confusion, the defilement of sin, and mental distraction.
Furthermore, there will be no disagreeable forms, nor any sounds, odors, tastes, or tactile objects—none of these evil sensory realms;
there will be no bad dreams;
and there will be no faults of the afflictions such as a woman’s greed, deception, flattery, crookedness, and jealousy.
Fully upholding the pure prohibitions and precepts, he practiced the ten paths of wholesome action;
he did not give rise to lustful thoughts toward others, nor was there anyone else who could conceive such lustful intentions toward the Noble Queen.

In the city of Kapilavastu, as well as in various villages and other lands, all men and women—whether boys or girls—who were possessed by ghosts or spirits were spontaneously healed upon seeing the Bodhisattva’s mother.

There may be sentient beings who suffer from various ailments—wind, bile, phlegm, or gas disorders; blindness, deafness, muteness, or paralysis; tooth decay and pain; scrofula, white leprosy, consumption, thirst, epilepsy, or vertigo; goiters, boils, sores, or scars. Upon seeing the Bodhisattva’s mother extend her hand to stroke their heads, these various diseases are naturally eliminated.

Should there be sentient beings who contract such illnesses and are unable to come in person to see the Bodhisattva’s mother, the Noble Queen at that time would break off blades of grass to fashion counting-sticks (śalākā) and bestow them upon them; as soon as they grasp the stick, all their painful afflictions were entirely dispelled, and they were restored to their original health.

When the Holy Queen beheld the Bodhisattva within her womb, she saw him dwelling at her right flank as clearly as one perceives various forms in a bright mirror; filled with joy and serenity, her body and mind were profoundly at ease.
“Ānanda! When the Bodhisattva dwelt in the womb, the devas constantly played celestial music and rained down various heavenly flowers as offerings to the Bodhisattva.

At that time, the realm was peaceful and the seasons were harmonious; the people lived in peace and happiness, delighting in the practice of benevolence. All the Śākya clansmen abandoned evil and cultivated wholesome deeds; during festivals and gatherings, they enjoyed themselves in the gardens and groves, experiencing supreme and wondrous pleasures with joy and serenity.”
At that time, King Śuddhodana followed the practice of the Dharma and took no pleasure in worldly glory; he abandoned his state affairs like an ascetic.
Ānanda! Such was the manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s supernatural power while dwelling within his mother’s womb.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"You all should contemplate the Jewel-Adorned Palace where the Buddha resided while in the womb.
Ānanda replied:
“Indeed so, World-Honored One!
We pray that you will reveal it for us.

Thereupon, the World-Honored One revealed to Ānanda, Śakra Devānām Indra, the four world-protectors, and the other devas and humans the precious, adorned palace where the Tathāgata dwelt while in the womb.
All were filled with great joy, attaining an unprecedented state and giving rise to a pure mind.
Having manifested this, the Great Brahma King took his precious palace and returned to the Brahma world.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"While the Bodhisattva was dwelling in the womb, he was already able to transform and guide thirty-six nayutas of devas and humans, causing them to abide in the Three Vehicles."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning, spoke in verse:
“When the Supreme and Most Excellent Person first enters the womb, The great earth, mountains, and forests all tremble.
His pure golden light dissolves the evil realms, And all devas and humans are filled with joy.”
Desiring to fulfill the role of this Great Dharma King, he manifested within the womb a palace adorned with jewels—
the jeweled palace where the Guide dwells, exquisitely decorated with the wondrous fragrance of sandalwood.
The value of even a single portion of this incense is equal to all the precious jewels of the three thousandfold world system;
from below, a great lotus flower emerges, its height reaching as far as the Brahma realm.
The nectar-flavor received within the flower, which the Brahma King held forth to offer to the Bodhisattva—
among all the various living beings in the world, there is none who can digest even a single drop of its flavor.
Only those Bodhisattvas in their final existence Are able to obtain this food of ambrosia;
Through the power of merit accumulated over many kalpas, Those who partake find body and mind purified.
Śakra, Brahmā, and the four World-Protectors, Bow their heads and make offerings to the Teacher;
Serving him with prostrations and hearing the wondrous Dharma, They depart with joy after circumambulating him to the right.
Thus, the multitudes of Bodhisattvas from the ten directions, likewise drawn by their delight in the Dharma, sit upon thrones of radiant, manifold jewels.
Hearing the Mahāyāna teachings, they give rise to great joy;
conversing freely with one another and gazing at each other, they offer boundless praise before returning to their own lands.
Men and women from the four quarters, Bound and tormented by malevolent spirits,
With disheveled hair and bared bodies, their minds deranged— Upon seeing the Mother of Buddhas, they are all healed.
All yellow phlegm and epilepsy, blindness, deafness, muteness, and all manner of ailments—
when the Mother of Buddhas extends her hand to stroke their crowns, these many diseases are instantly dispersed.
There may be those who are gravely ill in distant lands; he breaks off grass to fashion counting-sticks and bestows them upon them.
When the sticks reach the sick, they immediately recover; there is no one in the world who does not receive his manifold blessings.
Because the King of Dharma-Medicians was within her womb, all suffering sentient beings attained peace and joy;
the Noble Queen beheld the Bodhisattva’s body as clearly as seeing the bright moon in the sky.
Their physical forms are subtle, exquisite, and most dignified; they dwell with joy and delight, their minds securely settled.
No longer disturbed by greed, hatred, or delusion, they are likewise free from craving, envy, and malice.
Not afflicted by hunger, thirst, cold, or heat, body and mind are serene and free from all distress;
humans and devas, above and below, behold one another, and musical instruments resound spontaneously without being struck.
The land is pure and tranquil, exceedingly peaceful; The retinue rejoices together, free from all affliction.
Because of this, dragons and devas send down timely rains; Grasses, trees, flowers, and fruits all flourish in full splendor.
Bestowing all that is required, the royal palace rained down precious jewels for seven days;
at that time, there was no one in want, just like Śakra’s Joyful Garden.
The King practiced the holy life and maintained pure precepts; though dwelling in palace halls, he was as if in a forest wild.
Because of this, the Noble Queen conceived the Bodhisattva, and the King would enter the inner quarters every day to personally comfort her.
The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra, Scroll Second;
The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra, Scroll Third.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Divākara of Central India, by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Seven: On Birth.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"When the Bodhisattva had completed ten months in the womb and was about to be born, thirty-two kinds of auspicious omens first appeared within the palace of King Śuddhodana:
First, all the great trees were laden with buds about to blossom.
Second, within all the ponds and pools, the utpala, kumuda, padma, and puṇḍarīka lotuses were all covered in their stamens.
Third, various small clusters of flowers burst forth but have not yet opened.
Fourth, there are naturally eight rows of precious trees.
Fifth, twenty thousand treasuries emerge from the earth.
Sixth, precious sprouts spontaneously grew within the royal palace.
Seventh, immeasurable jeweled vases filled with fragrant oil emerged from the earth.
Eighth, immeasurable lion cubs came from the Snowy Mountains to circumambulate the city of Kapilavastu; leaping for joy and roaring, they each stood guard at the city gates.
Ninth, those lions likewise did not harass or harm any of the people.
Tenth, five hundred young white elephants came from the Snowy Mountains and arrived before the king’s palace.
Eleventh, immeasurable celestial infants suddenly appeared, being held and cradled by court ladies as they played and turned about.
Twelfth, various nāga maidens manifested half their bodies, holding exquisite jeweled necklaces in their hands as they remained suspended in the air.
Thirteenth, ten thousand celestial maidens each holding peacock-feather fans appeared in the sky.
Fourteenth, ten thousand precious vases, filled with scented water and floating with various flowers, appeared in the void and circled the city of Kapilavastu.
Fifteenth, ten thousand celestial maidens each holding a precious vase appeared in the void.
Sixteenth, ten thousand celestial maidens each holding banners, streamers, and precious parasols appeared in the void.
Seventeenth, immeasurable celestial maidens holding divine musical instruments appeared in the void of space, yet they did not strike or play them.
Eighteenth, all the fragrant winds remained still and motionless, without blowing or stirring.
Nineteenth, the waters of the rivers and streams became still and ceased to flow.
Twentieth, the palaces of the sun and moon, as well as all the stars and constellations, ceased their movements.
Twenty-first, the constellation Puṣya was about to be in conjunction with the moon.
Twenty-second: the palace halls of the royal residence were naturally covered by jeweled nets.
Twenty-third: all lamps and torches became colorless.
Twenty-fourth: upon all the multi-storied pavilions, halls, terraces, and turrets, mani-jewels suddenly appeared, suspended as magnificent ornaments.
Twenty-fifth: the treasuries of various jewels opened spontaneously of their own accord.
Twenty-sixth, all evil birds and strange beasts remain silent.
Twenty-seventh, from within the void, wondrous sounds and words are proclaimed, crying out: "Well-born! Well-born!"
Twenty-eighth: all human activities and undertakings come to a complete standstill.
Twenty-ninth: high and low ground becomes entirely level and even.
Thirtieth: all streets, lanes, alleys, and pathways for travel shall naturally become soft, strewn with flowers, and magnificently adorned.
Thirty-first: all pregnant women shall give birth without difficulty and attain complete peace and security.
Thirty-second: the deity of the *śāla* tree appeared with half her body revealed, joining her palms in reverent salutation.
First, these thirty-two kinds of auspicious signs appeared.
At that time, by the majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva, the noble Queen Māyā immediately knew that the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
During the first watch of the night, he went to King Śuddhodana and spoke these verses:
"Great King, listen to my request now: I have long desired to go to that Lumbinī Garden.
Do not harbor thoughts of resentment or jealousy toward me; I pray that I may go quickly for a brief excursion."
Great King, you have diligently contemplated the Dharma and practiced various austerities until you were weary;
yet since I conceived this pure being, he has resided within the palace for a long time.
The trees are lush and flourishing in their first bloom; now is the very time to enjoy the gardens.
As the season is spring and exceedingly beautiful, one may delight with the various court ladies.
Flocks of birds warble in harmony as if chanting hymns, And flying blossoms fill every place to overflowing;
I only pray that Your Majesty will swiftly issue an edict, To visit those beautiful gardens at this opportune time.
Having heard these words from the Noble Queen, the King was filled with joy and immediately commanded his ministers and aides:
"Quickly prepare the most exquisite palanquins and carriages, and likewise adorn Lumbinī Garden."
Furthermore, it is fitting to mount twenty thousand elephants, white in color like snow and shaped like mountains;
their bodies are resplendent with mani-jewels, and nets of pure gold thread are spread over them.
The elephant kings were all endowed with six tusks, with precious bells hanging down on both sides;
furthermore, twenty thousand swift and fleet horses were taken, with vermilion manes and white bodies like silver or snow.
He was equipped with a golden saddle, precious bells, and decorative nets; his horse galloped as swiftly as the wind.
His twenty thousand elite soldiers were all valiant and robust, capable of subduing hostile enemies and providing a secure defense.
Each donned armor and brandished spears and halberds, while simultaneously grasping battle-wheels and nooses;
the various litters and carriages upon which the Holy Queen rode were adorned with a mosaic of mani-jewels and diverse precious gems.
Furthermore, he loaded various exquisite delicacies onto chariots, covering them with exquisite cloths;
he also deployed chariot-warriors of great prowess, clad in armor and grasping various weapons.
Furthermore, he drove forth immeasurable vehicles, laden with rare and diverse precious jewels;
with boundless exquisite gems, he adorned and polished the Lumbinī Garden on every side.
Furthermore, with precious jewels and fine silks, he adorned the beautiful groves within the garden;
everywhere they were strewn with famous flowers, like the Joyful Garden of Śakra.
"Once you have prepared all these various items, you must immediately come and report to me.
Having received the king's command, the ministers promptly procured the materials and completed all the preparations.
The attendant reported:
"O King, Most Victorious in Fortune and Longevity, all that was commanded has been gathered.
Hearing these words, the king’s heart rejoiced; he immediately entered the inner chambers and issued an edict to the women of the palace:
"If you can love and follow me, you all should adorn yourselves completely with fragrant incense,
silken fabrics, and exquisite garments— soft, subtle, and pleasing to the heart."
Adorning their bodies with pearl pendants and necklaces, each holding hundreds of thousands of musical instruments—
zithers, lutes, flutes, pipes, and harps— they shall produce wondrous sounds through their drumming and blowing.
Should gods or humans, men or women, hear this, may they all feel love and joy;
as for the precious carriage in which the Noble Queen sits, let no other person be permitted to approach it.
The various court ladies took up the reins to drive the chariot; all inauspicious signs were completely cleared away.
The fourfold army gathered at the king’s gate, its deep rumbling like the sound of ocean waves.
Once the Holy Queen had first departed from the palace gates, all sang auspicious and sublime verses;
the palanquins and royal carriages were naturally adorned, while precious bells and chimes vibrated with harmonious sounds.
Thereupon, hundreds of thousands of devas and humans prepared lion thrones above;
alongside the chariot, four jeweled trees were arrayed, their branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all flourishing and lush.
Furthermore, there were auspicious birds with harmonious and elegant songs, fluttering, dancing, and gathering in flight;
banners, streamers, canopies, nets, and celestial garments rose high, surrounding and adorning the space everywhere.
The celestial maidens in the void offered praise with hearts full of joy;
at that moment, the Noble Queen ascended her precious carriage, and the three-thousandfold world-system shook in six ways.
Śakra purified the road, and the Four World-Protecting Kings came to drive the chariot;
Great Brahmā Deva acted as the vanguard, clearing away all evil omens.
Countless hundreds of thousands of devas paid homage with reverence and gazed up at him;
seeing these celestial hosts coming as his retinue, the father-king’s heart was filled with great joy.
He thought to himself:
"That which the Holy Queen bears in her womb must surely be a God among Gods; for he will be the Four World-Protecting Kings, Śakra, Brahmā, and the hosts of all the devas."
Having extensively established boundless great offerings, one will certainly attain Buddhahood through this;
among all sentient beings within the three realms, there is none capable of receiving such offerings.

Even if Śakra, Brahmā, and all the nāgas, along with the Four World-Protectors and others, were to receive this offering, they would be unable to sustain it and their heads would shatter; or, because of this offering, they might even meet their end.
"Only the Most Victorious One, God among Gods, is worthy of receiving the sublime offerings of gods and humans.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"At that time, there were eighty-four thousand elephant troops, cavalry, chariot troops, and infantry; all were handsome, brave, and invincible. Clad in armor and variously adorned, they held up weapons to protect the Holy Queen."
Sixty thousand Śākya maidens attended and surrounded him, while his kinsmen, both old and young, reverently guarded him.

Furthermore, there were sixty thousand royal consorts who performed various songs, music, dances, and theatrical displays; additionally, there were eighty-four thousand celestial maidens, eighty-four thousand nāga maidens, eighty-four thousand gandharva maidens, eighty-four thousand kiṃnara maidens, and eighty-four thousand asura maidens—all of whom adorned themselves with various jewels and performed manifold musical instruments, songs, dances, and hymns of praise. Attending upon the Mother of the Buddha as she proceeded to the Lumbinī Garden, they sprinkled excellent fragrant water over the entire ground and scattered celestial flowers. The grasses, trees, and shrubs within the garden—whether in season or out of season—had their branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all flourishing and ripened; its magnificent adornments were as extraordinary as Śakra’s Garden of Delight (Nandana).

"At that time, once the Noble Queen had reached the garden, she wandered through and observed it in detail until she came to the *pārijāta* jewel tree. Its branches and leaves were lush, verdant, and glistening; celestial flowers and human flowers bloomed all around it. A gentle breeze stirred them, releasing a fragrant scent, and it was further adorned with various colored *maṇi* jewels."

The ground beneath the tree was level as the palm of a hand; the various grasses that grew there were a deep azure color like the tail feathers of a peacock, and they produced a pleasant touch like that of kācilinda cloth. The mothers of immeasurable Buddhas of the past had all likewise come to sit beneath this precious tree.

At that time, hundreds of thousands of Śuddhāvāsa devaputras, their minds serene, some with braided hair hanging down and others wearing jeweled crowns, gathered beneath this tree and surrounded the Noble Queen. With joy, they prostrated and played celestial music to praise her; then, by the majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva, the branches and trunk of the tree bent low, whereupon they bowed their heads and paid homage at the feet of the Noble Queen.

At that time, the Noble Queen emitted a radiance from her body like lightning in the sky; looking up at the tree, she grasped an eastern branch with her right hand, stretched and yawned, and stood there with dignified grace.
At that time, sixty million celestial maidens from the desire realm arrived at the place of the Noble Queen to serve and make offerings to her.
Bhikṣus, you should know:

while dwelling in the womb, the Bodhisattva accomplished the various meritorious qualities and supernatural manifestations described above; having completed ten months, he was born peacefully from his mother’s right side, with right mindfulness and right awareness, free from any defilement or attachment.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"At that time, Śakra and Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, out of reverence and respect, bowed forward with bodies bent low; with single-minded right mindfulness, they immediately covered the Bodhisattva with two hands holding fine *kauśeya* silk, receiving and supporting him."
When those tasks were completed, he returned the precious palace in which the Bodhisattva had resided during his stay in the womb to the Brahma Heaven.
At that time, having been born, the Bodhisattva surveyed the four directions, looking about with composure and dignity, like a lion or a great man.
"Monks, you should know!

Having accumulated roots of goodness over many lifetimes, the Bodhisattva at that time attains the pure divine eye (*divyacakṣus*) and perceives all the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world systems, including their lands, cities, towns, and all sentient beings, fully understanding all their mental activities."
Having known this, he further observed whether the precepts, meditative concentration, wisdom, and various roots of goodness possessed by these sentient beings were equal to his own;
he then saw that throughout the trichiliocosm of the ten directions, there was not a single sentient being who was his equal.

At that time, the Bodhisattva, through skillful reflection, weighing of circumstances, and right mindfulness, was able to walk seven paces to the east by himself without needing support; wherever his feet were set down, lotus flowers sprang forth.
At that time, the bodhisattva was without fear and without hesitation, speaking these words:
"I have attained all wholesome dharmas; I shall now expound them for the sake of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, he walked seven steps toward the south and spoke these words:
'Among gods and humans, I am worthy of receiving offerings.
Furthermore, he walked seven steps toward the west and spoke these words:"
"I am the most honored and the most supreme in the world; this is my final body, for I have brought an end to birth, old age, sickness, and death.
Furthermore, he walked seven steps toward the north and spoke these words:
"Among all sentient beings, I shall be the unsurpassed one."
"Furthermore, he walked seven steps toward the nadir and spoke these words: 'I shall subdue all the armies of Māra;

I shall extinguish all the instruments of suffering, such as the fierce fires of the hells; I shall bestow the great cloud of Dharma and rain down the great rain of Dharma, so that all sentient beings may fully experience peace and happiness.'"
"Furthermore, he walked seven steps toward the zenith and spoke these words:
'I shall be one who is gazed upon by all sentient beings.
When the Bodhisattva uttered these words, his voice was heard throughout the entire trichiliocosm."
"Monks, you should know!

Having accumulated roots of goodness throughout many lifetimes, the Bodhisattva attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in his final birth; it is the natural law that such supernormal transformations occur."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

At that time, all sentient beings were filled with joy and leaped for gladness; the great earth shook, yet none of the sentient beings felt any fear. Furthermore, all the medicinal trees that do not grow in season throughout the trichiliocosm flourished and grew lush.”

From the midst of the void, wondrous sounds issued forth; a fine rain descended, and various celestial flowers and fragrances fell like rain, while pearls, necklaces, and exquisite garments drifted down in profusion.

Furthermore, it fanned a harmonious and subtle fragrant breeze capable of producing pure, supple, and pleasant tactile sensations; free from clouds, mist, smoke, dust, and darkness, there was heard from within the void a clear and elegant Brahma-voice praising the various meritorious qualities of the Bodhisattva.
At that time, the Bodhisattva emitted a great radiance of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of various and diverse colors, which filled the trichiliocosm.
All sentient beings who encountered this light experienced peace and stability in body and mind, with unsurpassed joy.
The light of all suns and moons, the Great Brahma Kings, Śakra, the World Protectors, and all other devas and humans completely faded away.

At that time, all sentient beings were distanced from greed, anger, ignorance, sorrow, grief, and fear; they were also freed from unwholesome evils and karmic obstacles. All sentient beings suffering from illness were healed, those who were hungry and thirsty were fully satisfied, those who were insane, intoxicated, or deranged regained their composure, and those with impaired faculties attained perfection.

The poor obtained wealth, the bound were liberated, and all beings in the hells received respite; sentient beings among the animals ceased their intent to harm one another, and all sentient beings among the hungry ghosts attained full satisfaction.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"By virtue of the power of his diligent cultivation of all wholesome deeds throughout incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, at the moment of his birth, the Bodhisattva was immediately able to take seven steps in each of the ten directions. Through the majestic empowerment of all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas, this ground was transformed into vajra, so that as the Bodhisattva walked upon it, it did not sink or crack."
At that time, the dark and gloomy regions between worlds were all filled with great radiance, and the sentient beings therein were each able to see one another.

Furthermore, at this moment, the celestial musicians produced subtle and wondrous sounds, and a rain of various heavenly flowers, powdered incense, and burning incense fell; flower garlands, precious jewels, various ornaments, and exquisite garments descended like clouds, so that all sentient beings attained supreme peace, stability, and happiness.

“The Bodhisattva’s appearance in the world is most honored and most supreme; all his merits enter the inconceivable, such that if one were to explain them in detail, they would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.
At that time, Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
When the Tathāgata was still a bodhisattva, he was already able to accomplish such supreme and rare feats; how much more so now that he has attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?

The Buddha told Ānanda: "In future ages there will be bhikṣus who are unable to cultivate bodily discipline, mental concentration, and wisdom; they will be foolish and ignorant, arrogant and conceited, agitated and distracted, failing to follow the Dharma and Vinaya. Greedy for much and lacking faith in the True Dharma, they will possess the defilements of a śramaṇa while merely resembling a śramaṇa. When such bhikṣus hear that the Bodhisattva entered the womb in purity, they will be unable to believe or accept it; instead, they will gather together and maliciously slander him, saying:
'Though the Bodhisattva dwelt in the mother’s right side while in the womb and was not defiled by pus or blood, how could he possibly possess such great merit?'"

"In this way, such foolish people are unable to know that the Bodhisattva has accumulated merit, nor can they know that the Bodhisattva manifests entry into the womb, yet possesses such supreme, pure, and immeasurable merit, appearing in the world out of compassion for sentient beings."

Ānanda! When the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, appear in the world, they do not attain perfect enlightenment or turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma in the heavens; rather, they manifest the attainment of Buddhahood only among human beings.
Why is this? If one were to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* among the devas, sentient beings among humans would all think:
"Since we are not devas, how could we possibly be capable of practicing the Buddha-way?"
Thereupon, he felt discouraged.
For this reason, he attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* only among human beings.
Yet those foolish ones, who are like thieves of the Dharma, are unable to comprehend the inconceivable deeds of a Bodhisattva; they thus give rise to slander and engage in groundless conjecture.
Ānanda! Even foolish people do not believe that the Buddha possesses immeasurable virtues, let alone being able to believe in the supernormal powers of a bodhisattva.
Such bhikṣus are attached to gain and fame, and are submerged in the defilement of sin.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
In future ages, if there are such ignorant and inferior persons who slander this sutra, how much sin will they incur?”
"Where will they be reborn?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If in future ages there are such evil bhikṣus who slander this sūtra, they will accumulate manifold sins and depart from the dharma of the śramaṇas."

Ānanda! Suppose there were a person who extinguished the Bodhi of the Buddha and reviled all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time—would the transgression they incur not be great?
Ānanda said,
"Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If there are sentient beings who slander such Mahāyāna sūtras as these, the transgression they incur shall be equal to that of this person.
At that time, having heard these words, Ānanda’s body hair stood on end, and he cried out: "Namo Buddhāya!"
“Namo Buddhāya!
Having heard that this person has committed such evil, my body and mind are overcome with confusion and distress.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“If there are sentient beings who destroy the Buddha’s bodhi, by reason of these evil deeds, they shall fall into the Avīci Great Hell. Ānanda!
In future ages, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who slander such Mahāyāna sūtras as these; when their lives end, they will certainly fall into the Avīci Great Hell.
Ānanda! You should not set limits to the virtues of the Tathāgata. Why is this?
Because the merit of the Tathāgata is profoundly deep, vast, and difficult to fathom, Ānanda!

If there should be anyone who hears this sutra and, with faith, acceptance, and love, gives rise to a heart of joy, such persons shall immediately attain pure livelihood and obtain great benefit. Their life will not have been spent in vain; they shall have cultivated wholesome conduct and attained the truth. They will leave behind the three evil realms and become true sons of the Buddha. Having attained profound faith, they are worthy of receiving offerings; their minds will be pure toward all noble sages, and they shall surely sever all nets of Māra. Thus able to emerge from the wilderness of birth and death, they will pull out the arrows of affliction, skillfully know where to take refuge, and obtain supreme and wondrous bliss.
Such persons as these are exceedingly rare; they are worthy of serving as the unsurpassed field of merit for the world. Why is this?
Because they are able to believe in the Dharma of the Buddhas, which is profoundly deep and difficult to believe.
Ānanda, you should know that this person did not achieve such faith through few roots of goodness. Why is this?
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, have previously served as spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to those people throughout many lifetimes. Ānanda!
If there are sentient beings who, though they have not yet seen the Buddha, the World-Honored One, give rise to faith and joy upon merely hearing his name;
Furthermore, there may be some who, having not heard the name of the Buddha, give rise to faith and joy upon seeing the Tathāgata;
or there may be some who, despite seeing and hearing [the Buddha], do not give rise to faith and joy;
or there may be some who give rise to faith and joy whether they hear or see [him].

Ānanda! Setting aside those who lack faith and joy, you should know that such persons, throughout many lifetimes, have all been sustained by the Tathāgata as their spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra). Their merit is equal to that of the Tathāgata; it is the Tathāgata himself who brings them to fulfillment and liberation, and who embraces them.
"Ānanda!
In the past, when I was practicing the bodhisattva path, whenever sentient beings came to me, I accepted them all and bestowed upon them fearlessness.
You all should now give rise to pure faith and practice with diligent effort."
That which you ought to do has been fully revealed, and I have also extracted for you all the arrows of pride. Ānanda!

Suppose there were a person who, after being long separated from a close friend, traveled more than a hundred yojanas at great risk to seek them out; upon meeting them, even the temporary relief from the thought of separation would bring joy—how much more so for one who has previously encountered a Buddha and planted roots of goodness, and now beholds the Buddha once again and becomes his intimate friend? How could such a person not rejoice?
Ānanda, you should know that all future Buddhas will think:
"These people have already taken past Tathāgatas as their spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), and now they have encountered me."
"I am also a close friend to this person, and my heart is filled with joy.
It is like someone who feels joy upon seeing a friend, and likewise feels joy upon seeing a friend's friend.
Ānanda! If there are sentient beings who give rise to even a small measure of faith in this sutra, I shall entrust these people to the Buddhas of the future.
Those Buddhas, in turn, will also form this thought:
"These sentient beings are my kinsmen and friends; I shall fulfill their wishes according to their desires.

It is, for example, like a man who has many kinsmen but who, having fathered an only son, feels profound affection for him. Before long, that man falls ill and is about to die; he calls his relatives together and entrusts this beloved son to them. Those friends receive the charge and cherish him as if he were their own son.
The Buddha is also like this.
All future Buddhas are his kinsmen and friends; for this reason, he entrusts these sentient beings to the future Buddhas. Ānanda!
"I have now awakened you; you should give rise to profound pure faith in this and diligently practice it.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"When the Bodhisattva was born, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of celestial maidens scattered divine, exquisite flowers, ointments, powdered incense, floral garlands, robes, and various ornaments over the Noble Queen, descending like clouds."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"About to give birth to the Stainless Light, sixty thousand celestial maidens all sang exquisite songs and hymns, praising the Bodhisattva’s mother."
Before the Noble Queen, they all spoke these words with joy:
"Please do not harbor grief or distress; we are capable of making offerings.
Your Majesty has given birth to One who has transcended the three realms, the Unsurpassed Great King of Physicians."
The flowers and leaves of the grasses and trees bloom; humans and devas alike pay him full homage.
The great earth quakes in six ways, and his fame spreads throughout the ten directions.
Such a most supreme person—the Noble Queen has now given birth to him.
The various musical instruments in the void resounded spontaneously without being struck;
hundreds of thousands of Śuddhāvāsa devas took refuge [in him] and were filled with joy.
Now that the Sage has appeared, he acts as a bridge and a ferry for the world.
The Four Kings, Śakra, Brahmā, and the rest of the hosts of devas,
bowing their bodies, surrounded him on all sides, and all gave rise to hearts of joy.
That Lion among Men was about to emerge from his mother’s right side.
The radiance is utterly pure, Its brilliance like a mountain of gold.
Śakra and Brahmā receive it upon their palms; It causes hundreds of thousands of worlds to tremble.
Sentient beings in the three evil realms Are freed from suffering and all find peace and joy.
Celestial garments and celestial flowers fill the void of space.
Through the power of the Buddhas' diligence, this earth becomes adamantine;
wherever the Guide sets foot, auspicious lotuses spring up at every step.
When he walked seven steps, he uttered a wondrous Brahma-voice:
"I am the Great King of Physicians, able to eliminate the disease of birth and death.
Within this world, I am the most honored and the most supreme."
The Brahmā, Śakra, and other devas, dwelling in the midst of space,
held fragrant water in their hands and sprinkled it upon the Bodhisattva;
the Dragon Kings sent down two streams of water, perfectly balanced in temperature, cool and warm.
The devas bathed the Bodhisattva with scented water;
the entire trichiliocosm trembled.
The devas held white parasols and grasped pure pearl necklaces.
Pervading the entirety of space, all adorned with jewels,
they held various kinds of offerings to worship the Lion among Men.
They reported to King Śuddhodana:
He shall increase the royal lineage, born from the kṣatriya clan,
destined to become a wheel-turning monarch who rules over the four continents.
It should be known that within the Śākya clan, five hundred sons will be born at that time.
"All are brave and robust, with strength like that of Nārāyaṇa.
Again, another reported to the king:
"Each of the male and female servants has borne eight hundred children; the mares have produced twenty thousand foals, and the cows have produced sixty thousand calves."
There were twenty thousand elephant cubs;
the kings of the various nations from the four quarters all offered congratulations at the same time, their number also being twenty thousand.
All the kings submitted themselves with devotion, bowing their heads and saying:
“Excellent, O Supreme King! I wish to be your servant.
The elephant king, adorned with a golden net, leaps for joy as it arrives at the royal palace;
the oxen are of various colors, upright and most lovely.”
A fine steed like white jade or snow, with mane and tail both golden in hue, brings further glory to the Great King’s lineage;
Your Majesty should go forth to behold it yourself.
All these manifold auspicious signs are due to the power of the Bodhisattva.
Seeing these meritorious deeds, the devas and humans all gave rise to hearts of joy;
they made vows to seek bodhi and swiftly ascend to the unsurpassed fruit.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"Once the Bodhisattva was born, King Śuddhodana further increased his practice of the Dharma, bestowing everything upon those who came to him in search of gifts.
At that same time, twenty thousand daughters were born into various noble families."
Among all the women, Yaśodharā was the foremost.
Furthermore, among the male and female servants and attendants, there were eight hundred sons and eight hundred daughters respectively; among all the sons, Chandaka was the most distinguished.
Twenty thousand fine horses were born as foals, among which Kanthaka was the foremost;
twenty thousand white elephant calves were also born.
Within the four hundred koṭis of continents, the sprouts of the Bodhi tree first appeared at that time, named Aśvattha.
Within the four continents, sandalwood groves grew;
on all four sides of Kapilavastu, five hundred gardens spontaneously appeared, and five thousand treasuries surged forth from the earth.
Regarding all the items mentioned above, the relevant departments were instructed to prepare them for the Bodhisattva’s service.
At that time, King Śuddhodana gathered with his kinsmen and thought to himself:
"Since my son was born, all these things have increased and been brought to fulfillment; I shall therefore give my son the name Sarvārthasiddha."
He then immediately offered various garments, food, and drink to celebrate the Bodhisattva’s new name.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“After the Bodhisattva was born, the Holy Mother’s right side returned to its former state, just as it had been before.”
From within a single well, three springs emerged to bathe the Bodhisattva’s mother; furthermore, exquisite fragrant oils issued from a pond for the Noble Queen to anoint her body.
Five hundred thousand celestial maidens, each holding a precious vase and carrying fine fragrant oils, came to where the Noble Queen was and greeted her, saying:
"May you give birth to a child in safety; may you suffer no injury."
Furthermore, there were five hundred thousand celestial maidens, each holding exquisite ointments, who anointed the body of the Holy Queen and comforted her, saying:
"May you give birth to a child in safety; may you suffer no injury."
Furthermore, there were five hundred thousand celestial maidens, each holding exquisite heavenly garments; for the sake of making offerings to the Bodhisattva, they asked the Noble Queen:
"May you give birth to a child in safety, and may you suffer no injury."
Furthermore, there were five hundred thousand celestial maidens, each holding precious ornaments; for the sake of making offerings to the Bodhisattva, they asked the Noble Queen:
"May you give birth to a child in safety, and may you suffer no injury."

Furthermore, there were five hundred thousand celestial maidens, each holding exquisite musical instruments for drumming, blowing, stringing, and singing; for the sake of making offerings to the Bodhisattva, they asked the Noble Queen:
"May you give birth to a child in safety, and may you suffer no injury."
Then all the non-Buddhist ṛṣis of the five supernatural powers in this Jambudvīpa traveled through the air to King Śuddhodana’s palace and addressed the king, saying:
"Your Majesty has fathered a son of merit; his auspiciousness is immeasurable and his lineage shall flourish."
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"After the Bodhisattva was born, for seven days and seven nights in the Lumbinī Grove, humans and devas played various kinds of exquisite music as offerings, showing him respect and praise; furthermore, they provided all manner of superior and wonderful food and drink."

The kinsmen of the Śākya clan all assembled together and proclaimed their auspiciousness; they practiced extensive giving and performed various meritorious deeds, making offerings to thirty-two thousand brahmins of renowned excellence and wisdom, satisfying them with whatever they required.
The Brahma King and Śakra transformed themselves into the forms of handsome māṇavas and sat upon the foremost seats within the assembly, chanting auspicious and subtle praises.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“When the Bodhisattva had been born, Maheśvara addressed the devaputras of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven, saying:
‘The Bodhisattva has already practiced the perfection of giving for hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya koṭi-nayuta kalpas.’”
Through generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, and extensive learning;
by accomplishing great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; with a mind that constantly aspires to benefit all beings;
having deeply planted roots of goodness under past Buddhas and being born from them; and by—
Adorned by the marks of a hundred blessings, courageous and resolute, he practiced all virtuous deeds and subdued the hosts of Māra and his enemies.
Having already accomplished pure and wondrous vows, he was named the Banner of Great Wisdom;
within the trichiliocosm, he served as a great guide, receiving offerings from devas and humans, and accumulating merit until it increased.
With noble aspirations, he will be far removed from birth, old age, sickness, and death;
he will reach the ultimate limit and be born into the Ikṣvāku lineage, before long attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and awakening the world.

I shall go there together with you all to offer them worship, reverence, respect, and praise; and furthermore, in order to eliminate the pride and agitation of the other devas, so that those gods may obtain benefit, attain peace and happiness, and realize awakening throughout the long night.
"Furthermore, I wish to see King Śuddhodana, to praise and celebrate his lineage with auspiciousness, and to proclaim that the Bodhisattva will certainly attain Buddhahood.

At that time, the Devaputra Maheśvara, surrounded by twelve hundred thousand celestial hosts, his radiance blazing and illuminating the city of Kapilavastu, went to the palace of King Śuddhodana. He prostrated before the Bodhisattva, circumambulated him one hundred thousand times, and reverently supported him.
He congratulated King Śuddhodana, saying:
"Great King, you should feel great joy. Why is this?

The King’s crown prince was adorned with the marks and signs of excellence; among all the devas and humans in the world, his physical appearance, radiance, moral virtue, and fame were preeminent in every respect.
"O Great King!
Such a bodhisattva will certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Thus it was, O bhikṣus!

Maheśvara and the devaputras of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens established a great offering and proclaimed that the Bodhisattva would certainly attain Buddhahood, after which they returned to their own abodes.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"Seven days after the Bodhisattva’s birth, Queen Māyā passed away and was reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."

After seven days had passed, the Bodhisattva returned to the city of Kapilavastu; the ceremonies and magnificent adornments were even more extraordinary than those when he had gone to the Lumbinī Garden with the Noble Queen.
There were five hundred thousand celestial maidens, each holding a precious vase filled with scented water;
five hundred thousand court ladies followed in succession, each holding a peacock-feather fan;
and five hundred thousand court ladies walked ahead, sprinkling scented water upon the ground as they led the way.
Five hundred thousand celestial maidens walked ahead, holding brooms to sweep the ground;
five hundred thousand court ladies followed in succession, their bodies adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments;
five hundred thousand celestial maidens followed in succession, holding precious flower garlands.
Five hundred thousand maidens, carrying various precious vessels, proceeded in succession;
